_comment: Proposed replacement home page for the default scene. A design document,
not a scene: run tools/check_board_words.py over it before it becomes one.
The principle is the one the diff against Aubrey's board exposed: our home
page is a sampler of every category, hers is a surface for building a
sentence. Category CONTENTS move behind the links that already exist, and
the freed cells buy the verbs and function words a sentence actually needs.
Clusters are contiguous in reading order rather than placed in fixed
columns, because the grid is a flow layout and column position is not
stable across devices. Reading order is the only spatial promise we can
keep on every screen, so the clustering has to live there.
Every cluster is ONE colour. That is the actual content of Brandi's advice:
clustering by part of speech only teaches anything if the block reads as a
block. An earlier draft grouped by meaning instead - 'quantity and
negation' together - and the checker caught that it spanned grey, red, blue
and pink, which is four blocks wearing one label.
Links are one contiguous run at the top. Brandi offered two options -
colour each folder to match its category, or keep them uniform and put
them all in one row. The first does not survive contact with our pages:
'people' holds both nouns (mom, student) and pronouns (I, you), so there
is no single correct colour for the folder that opens it.

clusters.name: pronouns (yellow) — who the sentence is about, first in reading order
verbs (green) — the engine; all of these are currently buried behind the actions link
negation (red) — deliberately its own colour, and adjacent to nothing else
social (pink) — the few that earn a home-page cell rather than a link
describe (light blue) — the two highest-frequency modifiers
